1. (Judgment 2) At 1440 the Lions 45–21 tile overlaps the hero: the final T of "IMPORTANT" runs under the tile's left edge. Pull the tile outward on its radius, or narrow the centred column, so every hero line sits clear of the orbit tiles.
2. (Judgment 5) The Spaceman card reads "The company that proved an idea could carry all the way through — built, funded and shipped as founder… a product in the market that stood on its own." The record describes Spaceman as the LLC Doug has operated under since 2018 for independent design and engineering work, partnering with companies and studios. It mentions no funding and no single market product. Replace the text with copy drawn from the record.
3. (Judgment 4) At 360, fold 1 shows the top of the Lions 45–21 tile below the attribution, but `first_fold` declares only the hero phrase and the mark in the first 640px. Push the orbit stack below the fold so the statement carries fold 1 alone.

1. (Judgment 5) The Spaceman card says "partnering with companies and studios to carry projects from the brief all the way to a finished ship." The records don't make that claim. They say Spaceman partners "with companies and studios across industries" on "product design, frontend engineering, design systems, and brand — sometimes as a solo contributor, sometimes embedded in a larger team." Replace the brief-to-ship line with wording taken from the record.

2. (Judgment 3) At 1440 the four tiles sit at roughly equal distance from the statement, one in each quadrant. The radial order the brief intends (Lions nearest, Baycurrent mid-ring, market furthest and faintest) doesn't read. The SPY tile sits upper-left, as close to the hero as the Lions tile. Its light tan figure on a dark surface also makes it one of the more legible tiles, not the faintest. Push the market tile out to the far edge and set its text in `textFaint`. Pull the Lions tile in closest to the line.

1. (Judgment 2/3) At 1440 the gold Lions 45-21 tile sits on top of the hero. It cuts "IMPORTANT" to "IMPORTA" and "HOW WE" to "HOW W", so the phrase meant to lead is partly hidden behind a satellite. Move the orbit radius out until the tile clears the statement's ~22ch column. The tiles should orbit the finish, not cover it.
2. (Judgment 2/3) At 1440 the Baycurrent Classic tile covers the "S" of "START, BUT", so the hero reads "TART, BUT". Push this tile clear of the centred column as well, so every word of the phrase is intact.
